business_problem: Magna needed to improve efficiency, safety and agility across its global manufacturing operations while also helping its autonomous delivery vehicle platform adapt to new cities and complex physical environments.
solution_summary: Magna describes an operational AI program that spans factory automation and autonomous delivery. In manufacturing, the company feeds sensor data, robot workflows and camera streams into AI systems for predictive maintenance, quality inspection, pick-and-place automation, and factory-layout simulation under its Factory of the Future strategy. For its City Delivery autonomous vehicle, Magna is evaluating NVIDIA Cosmos Reason as the reasoning vision-language model that can interpret physical environments and help the vehicle adapt to new cities and changing street conditions. Magna pairs that model with NVIDIA Omniverse simulation APIs and libraries so scenarios can be modeled and tested before field rollout, reducing development time and cost. The resulting stack connects factory and vehicle data sources to machine-learning, simulation, and embedded decision systems that support real-time operational AI across manufacturing and mobility.

data_flow: Across Magna operations, sensor data from equipment and factory processes feeds machine-learning-driven predictive maintenance, while camera inputs support computer vision for inspection and pick-and-place. For autonomous delivery, Magna uses NVIDIA Omniverse simulation APIs and libraries to simulate scenarios and pairs them with NVIDIA Cosmos Reason so the City Delivery platform can reason about physical environments and execute decisions on embedded vehicle systems.
